findings.title: Two officer IDs do not establish two independent people
locations: contract/project.zeno: field 120 Caller.officer and Officer variants
contract/v2/policy.json: officer variable, recognized-officer and repeat-officer cases
reproduction: Select Bob from the same browser/operator and approve.
The local example records a release without asking for credentials.
findings.implication: This is expected under simulated identity. Deployment needs an authenticated caller adapter and role/key governance; a proof about enum values does not supply either.
findings.implemented_response: Main prose, UI, README and mental toolkit explicitly scope key to an approval by an ID, not a cryptographic signature or proof of two people.

findings.title: Destination deduplication is local to a MemoryDestination instance
reproduction: Call deliver_next_memory_unacknowledged twice with one MemoryDestination: one distinct delivery is recorded.
Call it with a fresh MemoryDestination: that instance records the same delivery again.
findings.observed: Same content-bound ID in every attempt; delivered_count is 1 in each fresh sink.
findings.implication: The case establishes one release intent per logical request history and same-sink retry behavior. Durable external exactly-once delivery is not established.
findings.implemented_response: The demonstration, native app description, essay and README distinguish outbox intent from real delivery and explicitly retain a durable destination as a separate obligation.

findings.title: Unkeyed history and trusted acknowledgements do not prevent hostile file rollback or forged delivery observations
reproduction: On a scratch database run the actual generated CLI with --decide; save a copy while pending=1.
Use a direct SQLite host write: UPDATE v2_deliveries SET acknowledged=1. The generated --audit reports pending=0.
Restore the saved valid pending database; --deliver reports one delivery.
Restore that same saved copy again; --deliver reports the same delivery ID again to its fresh recording sink.
findings.implication: Audit validates the stated history and checked contents; it does not authenticate the host observation that real delivery occurred or prove that a valid file is the newest one.
findings.implemented_response: Essay, app details and README explicitly preserve host integrity, external checkpoints and destination behavior as separate assumptions. No universal tamper-proof or rollback-proof claim remains.
